name: Leopold Lojka — The Chauffeur

choices: Watch the lead car carefully as it pulls away — note which direction it signals before moving
Turn briefly to Governor Potiorek in the jump seat and ask whether you have the correct route
Follow the lead car as ordered, maintaining your position in the motorcade
opening.narrative: It is half past ten on a Sunday morning in Sarajevo and the sun has burned through the last of the morning cloud. The Town Hall — its Moorish arches and ochre facade — is behind you; the Appel Quay opens ahead, the Miljacka river bright and cold to the south. The motorcade is six cars: the Chief of Police, then you, then four others carrying staff and security. The Archduke and Duchess are already seated behind you — you can hear the murmur of their voices, low and private, beneath the noise of the crowd. The lead car begins to move.

briefing: Your white gloves are on the wheel and the engine of the Gräf & Stift is running beneath you, a low vibration through the leather seat and the polished wood of the steering column. The Town Hall steps are behind you; the motorcade is forming up, and you are in your correct position — second car, directly behind the Chief of Police's vehicle, as you were briefed this morning before the procession began. The smell of exhaust and hot motor grease mixes with something sweeter from the direction of the quay, chestnut smoke or river air, and the brass band has not stopped playing. You heard the explosion earlier — a flat crack from somewhere ahead on the quay, then smoke, then the motorcade continuing — and no one has told you what it was or whether the route has changed. Your orders are the orders you received this morning: follow the lead car, obey the senior officer in your vehicle, bring the Archduke and Duchess safely to their destination. The lead car's engine note changes as it begins to move. Your right hand rests on the gear lever. You are waiting for the car ahead of you to give you your direction.
description: You drive the Archduke's car. You follow orders and you follow the car ahead of you. You do not know, yet, that those two things are about to pull the century off its hinges.
perspective: Write from the perspective of a skilled professional whose expertise is mechanical and procedural — a man who knows his car intimately and his orders exactly, and who experiences the event as a sequence of professional decisions made in good faith under incomplete information. No false foreknowledge. No dramatic irony from inside his perspective. The horror is in the gap between what he knows and what the player knows.
character_hooks: I have driven this route twice in practice runs this week — I know every corner, and Franz Josef Street was never on the itinerary.
The reverse gear gave me trouble yesterday on a wet cobbled hill near the Konak — I mentioned it to the mechanic, but there was no time to adjust it before this morning.
I overheard two officers speaking on the Town Hall steps — something about a changed route to the hospital — but they moved away before I could hear the details, and no one has spoken to me directly.
context_sentence: You are Leopold Lojka, the Archduke's chauffeur, and the car ahead of you is moving.

inventory: route briefing card — original route only
mechanical knowledge of the Gräf & Stift transmission

startingKnowledge: The original briefed route: Appel Quay to the Latin Bridge and back to the Konak
That a grenade was thrown at the motorcade earlier this morning — you heard it and saw the smoke
The mechanical characteristics of the Gräf & Stift's transmission, including the stiffness of the reverse gear under hard braking
That Governor Potiorek is in the jump seat directly behind you and is the senior authority in the car
